info.description: API documentation for the bridge tracker service
info.title: Bridge Tracker API

get.description:
Scans every bridge service the tracker knows about for bridges sent by
from_address and reports each one's claim state, exactly as the bridge service
reported it. Results are cached: a bridge already known to be claimed, with its
claim record already fetched, is not rechecked on a later call. Passing
includeTracking=true additionally registers every still-unclaimed bridge with
the bridge tracker and includes its current tracking snapshot. filterBridges
restricts the result to bridges with only that claim state (claimed / still
pending / errored while checking). A network whose bridge service could not be
scanned is skipped and reported in the "warnings" field instead of failing the
whole request.
get.summary: Get bridge activity by sender address

parameters.description: Address that sent the bridges to look up
parameters.name: from_address

parameters.description: Register still-unclaimed bridges with the tracker
parameters.name: includeTracking

500.description: Scanning the configured bridge services failed

get.description:
With no network_id, reports the bridge contract address of every network the
tracker currently knows about (via the bridge service finder). With network_id,
reports only that network's.
get.summary: Get the bridge contract address of one network, or every network

500.description: Resolving the bridge contract address failed

With no network_id, reports the bridge contract address of every network the

get.description:
Returns the health status, instance identity and build information of the
running instance. Useful as liveness/readiness probe and to check which
build/configuration runs on each instance behind the proxy

Returns the current step of the bridge and the full path it is expected to
follow. Calling this endpoint adds the bridge to the list of supervised
bridges. The response is always a TrackingData: its bridge_status field is
null until the tracker resolves the bridge, so the client keeps polling (or
subscribes over the WebSocket) until it is populated
get.summary: Get bridge status by transaction hash

parameters.description: Network where the bridge transaction was sent (0 -> Mainnet)
parameters.name: network_id

parameters.description: Hash of the transaction that created the bridge (bridgeAsset or bridgeMessage)
parameters.name: tx_hash

200.description: Bridge registered; bridge_status/error fill in once resolved

400.description: Invalid transaction hash or network id

bridge.description:
Bridge is the raw bridge event, exactly as returned by the origin network's bridge
service, unmodified

bridge_network_id.description:
BridgeNetworkID is the network whose bridge service reported Bridge — not necessarily
Bridge.OriginNetwork, which is the origin network of the bridged asset and can differ for
a re-bridged asset (see domain.ScannedBridge)

claim.description:
Claim is the raw claim record, exactly as returned by the destination network's bridge
service, unmodified, once Claimed is true and the indexer has recorded it

claim_network_id.description:
ClaimNetworkID is the network whose bridge service reported Claim (the bridge's
destination network); only present alongside Claim

claimed.description:
Claimed is the tri-state result of the destination bridge contract's isClaimed() call
the last time it was checked: "false" (confirmed unclaimed), "true" (claimed), or
"error" if the check itself failed (e.g. no bridge contract address configured for the
destination network) — callers must not read "error" as "false"

creation_timestamp.description:
CreationTimestamp is when this bridge was first cached by the activity endpoint (unix
seconds); it never changes after that

errors.description:
Errors holds the message of whatever check failed the last time this item was refreshed,
keyed by which check it was — currently only "claim", present when Claimed is "error"

last_updated_timestamp.description:
LastUpdatedTimestamp is when this item's claim/tracking state was last (re)checked (unix
seconds), whether or not anything about it actually changed. Stops advancing once the
bridge is claimed with its claim record fetched — nothing left to recheck

tracking.description:
Tracking is the bridge tracker's current status for this bridge; only present when the
request set includeTracking=true and the bridge is still unclaimed

bridges.description: Bridges holds every bridge found for FromAddress across every configured bridge service

warnings.description:
Warnings lists every network whose bridge service could not be scanned this call; absent
when every configured network was scanned successfully. Bridges may be incomplete for the
networks listed here, but is still valid for every other network

message.description: Message is the error encountered while scanning NetworkID

network_id.description: NetworkID is the network whose bridge service could not be scanned

bridge_address.description: BridgeAddress is the bridge contract address on NetworkID

network_id.description: NetworkID is the network BridgeAddress belongs to

bridges.description: Bridges holds the bridge contract address of every network currently known

amount.description:
Amount is the amount of the asset being bridged, as a decimal string — a plain JSON
number would risk losing precision on wei-scale amounts in clients that decode numbers
as float64 (e.g. JavaScript)

deposit_count.description: DepositCount is the index of the bridge leaf in the origin exit tree

destination_address.description: DestinationAddress is the address that receives the asset on the destination network

destination_network.description: DestinationNetwork is the network the bridge exits to (0 -> Mainnet)

leaf_type.description: LeafType is the string representation of the kind of leaf the bridge created (asset or message)

origin_address.description: OriginAddress is the address of the asset on the origin network

origin_network.description: OriginNetwork is the network where the bridged asset originates from

block_number.description: BlockNumber is the block, on the origin network, where the BridgeEvent was emitted

block_timestamp.description: BlockTimestamp is the timestamp of the block, on the origin network, where the BridgeEvent was emitted

bridge_type.description: BridgeType is the string representation of the bridge's direction (e.g. "L1->L2")

event.description: Event holds the facts unpacked directly from the on-chain BridgeEvent log

log_index.description: LogIndex is the position of the BridgeEvent log within BlockNumber

error.description: Error carries the error details when Status is types.StepStatusError, nil otherwise

result.description:
Result is the data the step has produced so far; its shape depends on Step:
*types.GERUpdateResult (StepWaitingGERUpdate), *types.InjectedGERResult
(StepWaitingGERInjection), *types.LERUpdateResult (StepWaitingLERUpdate),
*types.PendingInclusionResult (StepPendingInclusion), *types.CertificateData
(StepCertificatePending), *types.L1SettledGERResult (StepWaitL1SettledGER),
*types.InjectedGERL1Leaf (StepWaitingL1InfoLeafAvailable) or *types.ClaimResult
(StepClaimed). nil until
the step produces one, and for steps that never do. Most steps only set this once Done,
but StepCertificatePending (Status still InProgress) may already carry the certificate's
current, not yet settled, status — see domain.ErrCertificateNotSettled

status.description: Status is the string representation of the step's status (e.g. "done")

step_index.description: StepIndex is this step's position within the parent TrackingData.AllSteps list

step_name.description: StepName is the string representation of the bridge step (e.g. "PendingInclusion")

all_steps.description:
AllSteps holds all expected steps of the bridge's route; GER/LER, certificate and
claim data are reported per step in each entry's Result. nil while BridgeStatus is nil

bridge_status.description:
BridgeStatus is nil until the tracker resolves the bridge; from then on it carries
the full BridgeStatus. Marshaled explicitly as null while unresolved (no omitempty)
so clients can poll on its presence without an extra field to check

claim_status.description:
ClaimStatus is a simplified claim-readiness summary, one of "pending",
"readyToClaim", "claimed" or "error" — see domain.TrackingData.ClaimStatus for exactly
how it is derived from TrackingStatus and the current step. For most clients this is all
that is needed to know whether the bridge can be claimed; TrackingStatus/AllSteps remain
for anything that needs the full detail

error.description:
Error mirrors whatever currently explains the bridge not progressing, if anything: a
terminal give-up to even resolve it (e.g. the tx does not exist on the network or is
not a bridge transaction — TrackingStatus is Error and BridgeStatus/StepIndex/AllSteps
stay nil forever), a transient FindBridge failure still being retried (TrackingStatus
is unaffected), or the same error already nested in AllSteps[StepIndex].Error once the
bridge is otherwise resolved. nil while nothing has failed

network_id.description: NetworkID is the network of the request (0 -> Mainnet)

step_index.description:
StepIndex is the index into AllSteps of the step that explains TrackingStatus: the
step currently in progress when Running, the step in error when Error, or the last
step (Claimed) when Finished. nil while BridgeStatus/AllSteps are nil

tracking_status.description: TrackingStatus is the string representation of the bridge's lifecycle status

tx_hash.description: TxHash is the transaction hash of the request

types.BridgeResponse.description: Detailed information about a bridge event

block_num.description: Block number where the bridge event was recorded

block_pos.description: Position of the bridge event within the block

block_timestamp.description: Timestamp of the block containing the bridge event

bridge_hash.description: Unique hash representing the bridge event, often used as an identifier

deposit_count.description: Count of total deposits processed so far for the given token/address

destination_address.description: Address of the token receiver on the destination network

destination_network.description: ID of the network where the bridge transaction is destined

from_address.description:
Address that initiated the transaction on bridge contract. It can be intermediary contract or EOA.
May be null if bridge was synced with SyncFromInBridges=false

global_index.description: Global index of the bridge event (consisted of mainnet flag, rollup id and deposit count)

leaf_type.description: Type of leaf (bridge event type) used in the tree structure

metadata.description: Optional metadata attached to the bridge event

origin_address.description: Address of the token sender on the origin network

origin_network.description: ID of the network where the bridge transaction originated

to_address.description: Address of the contract that was the recipient of the transaction. This may differ from the bridge contract address.

tx_hash.description: Hash of the transaction that included the bridge event

txn_sender.description: Address of the transaction sender who initiated the bridge transaction

types.ClaimResponse.description: Detailed information about a claim event

block_num.description: Block number where the claim was processed

block_timestamp.description: Timestamp of the block containing the claim

destination_address.description: Address receiving the claim on the destination network

destination_network.description: Destination network ID where the claim was processed

from_address.description: Address from which the claim originated

global_exit_root.description: Global exit root associated with the claim

is_message.description: IsMessage indicates whether this is a message claim (leaf type 1) rather than an asset claim (leaf type 0)

mainnet_exit_root.description: Mainnet exit root associated with the claim

origin_address.description: Address initiating the claim on the origin network

origin_network.description: Origin network ID where the claim was initiated

proof_local_exit_root.description: Proof local exit root associated with the claim (optional)

proof_rollup_exit_root.description: Proof rollup exit root associated with the claim (optional)

rollup_exit_root.description: Rollup exit root associated with the claim

tx_hash.description: Transaction hash associated with the claim

code.description: Code is an HTTP-like error code (e.g. 400 invalid params, 404 bridge tx not found)

message.description: Message is a human-readable description of the error

description.description: Description holds the human-readable description of the error; one entry per occurrence

error_type_string.description: ErrorTypeString is the string representation of ErrorType, auto-populated on JSON marshaling

retry_count.description: RetryCount is the number of retries attempted so far for this step

config_sha1.description:
ConfigSHA1 is the sha1sum (hex) of the configuration the instance was started with;
it allows checking that all instances behind a proxy run the same configuration

instance_id.description:
InstanceID is a UUID generated at startup; it changes on every execution, so two
responses with different InstanceID come from different instances (or the same
instance after a restart)

version.description: Version is the build/version information of the running instance

git_branch.description: GitBranch is the git branch the binary was built from

git_rev.description: GitRev is the git revision the binary was built from

go_version.description: GoVersion is the Go runtime version (e.g. "go1.24.0")

os.description: OS is the target operating system (e.g. "linux")
